# Project Bootstrap — Cursor + Claude Code + Codex Configuration Installer
**Version:** 30.0
**Last Updated:** 2026-07-21

This bootstrap is the single source of truth for a **GitHub-backed** project on any hosting platform (e.g. Railway, Vercel, Fly.io, AWS), using **Cursor Desktop** as the primary IDE and **Claude Code** and **OpenAI Codex** as companions for premium-tier planning, review, and optional execution work. Cursor runs on Ultra; Claude Code on the Max subscription; Codex on your ChatGPT subscription or API billing (CLI or IDE extension).

Replaces v20 `cursor-bootstrap.md` and v1.1 `claude-bootstrap.md` in a single file. Delete those files from your project root after running FULL INSTALL or UPDATE ONLY with v22 or later.

---

## How to use this file

Upload `bootstrap.md` into the **root of the project you already have open in Cursor**.

**v21 → v22 transition note.** v22 introduces the `Workflow Schema:` plan-file marker, the `Executor tier:` line recorded at the Executor Capability Gate (Step 0 of `/create-plan` and `/review-plan`), inline `Triage:` per Findings Log entry (replacing the standalone `## LOW Triage` section), severity-aware scope-expansion routing in `/review` / `/fix` / `/execute`, and `Risk if deferred:` + `Revisit by:` annotations on retained items. **Existing v21 plans continue to work in legacy mode** — v22 commands detect the absence of the `Workflow Schema:` marker and fall back to v21 field expectations. New plans created after UPDATE ONLY use the v22 schema. If v22 misbehaves in a downstream repo, revert via `git checkout <pre-v22-commit> -- .cursor/ .claude/` — v21 commands ignore any unknown v22 fields, so existing v22-shaped plan files continue to work in mixed mode.

**v22 → v22.1 sub-note.** v22.1 is a maintenance release of the artefact packaging — it does not change any `.cursor/` or `.claude/` payload behaviour. UPDATE ONLY from v22.0 to v22.1 is therefore **optional** for downstream projects; the embedded payload changes in this release are cosmetic only (the `/review.md` command's example text now references the unversioned `cursor-guide.md` / `.docx` filename instead of the old `cursor-guide-combined-v22.*` form). The user-facing reference at the top of this repo is now `cursor-guide.md` (and its regenerated `cursor-guide.docx`), with the optional Claude Code split-workflow companion folded in as Section 6.

**v22.1 → v22.2 sub-note.** v22.2 makes `/peer-review` plan-aware. A new `## Step 0 — Auto-detect plan, findings, and changed files` opener detects the active plan, reads the latest `/review`-sourced round in `Review Findings Log` (skipping any `peer-review`-sourced rounds), reads plan body context, discovers changed files via `git status` + `git diff`, and auto-fires the model-diversity warning when the targeted round's `Source:` matches the tool running `/peer-review`. A new 3-option fallback menu (describe / paste / read changed files) fires when auto-detect cannot proceed or the user opts out. A new `## Handoff — choose your path` wrap-up presents two paths at the end: (a) paste PR-* / PR-REG- findings to the executor for in-chat triage (default — preserves executor-verifies workflow); (b) write PR- findings to the Findings Log as round N+1 with `Source: Cursor peer-review` / `Source: Claude Code peer-review` on explicit opt-in (recommended when the executor session is gone, so `/fix` picks them up from disk with no paste). UPDATE ONLY from v22.0 or v22.1 to v22.2 is **RECOMMENDED** for downstream projects (contrast with v22.1, which was optional cosmetic-only) — without it, downstream projects don't get the new cross-tool ergonomics. The plan-file schema is unchanged (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`), so existing v22 plans and v21 plans (in legacy mode) continue to work without modification.

**v22.2 → v22.3 sub-note.** v22.3 folds a small behavioural refinement into the Step 0.3 / Step 3.4 clarification gates of `/create-plan` and `/review-plan` on both Cursor and Claude Code: ask clarifying questions one at a time, provide a recommended answer per question, wait for the user response before asking the next, and walk down the design tree resolving dependencies one decision at a time. No plan-schema change (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`); no new commands, rules, or templates. UPDATE ONLY from v22.0 / v22.1 / v22.2 to v22.3 is **optional** for downstream projects; the embedded payload changes in this release are limited to the 4 command files listed above plus the installer's own version header. Existing v22 / v21-legacy plans continue working unchanged.

**v22.3 → v22.4 sub-note.** v22.4 introduces the **Deferral Confirmation Gate** across `/create-plan`, `/review-plan`, `/execute`, `/review`, and `/fix` on both Cursor and Claude Code. The gate removes silent MED/LOW deferral paths and silent `Defer` / `Accept` skip paths: every would-be deferral or skip is presented one at a time with a recommendation, app-impact line, production-impact flag (new runtime dependency / new environment variable / database migration / deploy-side config change / dev/prod parity drift), and four choices — `Fix now`, `Include in plan`, `Defer`, `Accept`. Existing CRIT/HIGH inline hard-stops are preserved; empty batches are silent; aborted gates do not commit pending dispositions to disk. In `/execute`, MED/LOW scope-expansion accumulates as pending candidates that fire at the next natural pause point (recommended-checkpoint, hard-stop, or end-of-plan) rather than mid-task. In `/review`, the gate fires once after findings enumeration and before `Review Findings Log` append, covering `Triage: Defer` / `Triage: Accept` findings and MED/LOW scope-expansion dispositions; `Triage: Fix-now` / `Triage: Fix-now-if-tied` are not gated. In `/fix`, a new Step 1.5 gate confirms any disposition that would skip current fixing before `/fix` honours it, including overrides from Fix-now to Defer/Accept. No plan-schema change (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`); no new commands, rules, or templates. UPDATE ONLY from v22.0 / v22.1 / v22.2 / v22.3 to v22.4 is **RECOMMENDED** for downstream projects because it removes a known silent-deferral failure mode; the embedded payload changes are limited to the 10 affected command files plus the installer's own version header. Existing v22 / v21-legacy plans continue working unchanged.

**v22.4 → v22.5 sub-note.** v22.5 hardens `/review` so second and later review rounds remain full feature/change reviews, not just fix-verification passes. The Step 0.5 baseline is renamed to **primary review baseline** (defines the feature/change scope and the changed-files surface for the normal correctness / security / executor-judgment passes) and is kept distinct from the **regression baseline** used inside Post-Fix Regression Check (the pre-`/fix` state used only to catch fix-induced regressions). Prior review findings are explicitly reframed as context and focus guidance, not a code baseline and not a changed-files scope limiter — so round 2+ does not shrink to "files touched by the most recent `/fix`". The Post-Fix Regression Check is now marked **additive**: a clean run there does not substitute for the main review passes. `Smart Self-Check` is renamed to **Missed-Issue Pass (unconditional, auditable)** with a required output line in the shape `Missed-issue pass: re-read <files/regions>; result: <none | finding IDs>`, and the same line is added to the Summary block so the pass cannot be satisfied performatively. The plan-template `Scope-expansion disposition` example wording is cleared of the stale silent-default and silent-capture phrasing that contradicted the v22.4 Deferral Confirmation Gate. The same cleanup is extended to `/fix.md`'s LOW scope-expansion bullet on both Cursor and Claude Code, which is reframed as a legacy-only path with an explicit "(v21 silent-capture behaviour preserved for the legacy path)" note plus a v22.4+ precedence clarifier — so the bullet stops reading as the default v22.4+ behaviour. No plan-schema change (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`); no new commands, rules, or templates. UPDATE ONLY from v22.0 / v22.1 / v22.2 / v22.3 / v22.4 to v22.5 is **RECOMMENDED** for downstream projects because it removes the round-2+ "fix-verification only" failure mode in `/review`; the embedded payload changes are limited to the two `/review.md` command files, the two `/fix.md` command files, the plan template, and the installer's own version header. Existing v22 / v21-legacy plans continue working unchanged.

**v22.5 → v23.0 sub-note.** v23.0 adds **OpenAI Codex** as a first-class external-agent companion alongside Cursor and Claude Code. New install surface: 13 `.agents/skills/<name>-codex/SKILL.md` repo-scoped Codex Skills corresponding 1:1 to the Cursor and Claude Code companion command set (`start-session-codex`, `create-branch-codex`, `explore-codex`, `create-plan-codex`, `review-plan-codex`, `load-plan-codex`, `execute-codex`, `review-codex`, `peer-review-codex`, `fix-codex`, `document-codex`, `push-codex`, `end-session-codex`); 6 `.agents/skills/<name>-codex/agents/openai.yaml` metadata files setting `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` for the side-effecting Skills (`$execute-codex`, `$fix-codex`, `$push-codex`, `$end-session-codex`, `$create-branch-codex`, `$document-codex`); and a `.codex/config.toml` raising `project_doc_max_bytes` to 65536 so Codex reads the full `AGENTS.md` (above the documented 32 KiB default). FULL INSTALL and UPDATE ONLY now also create / refresh `.agents/skills/` and `.codex/config.toml` and verify `.agents/` and `.codex/` are not gitignored. Codex Skills are invoked explicitly with `$skill-name-codex` (e.g. `$execute-codex`, `$review-codex`) or selected via Codex's built-in `/skills` selector — this is distinct from Cursor's and Claude Code's `/skill-name` syntax (preserved unchanged for those tools). The `-codex` suffix on every Skill keeps slash menus unambiguous in tools that auto-discover `.agents/skills/` (notably Cursor 2.4+, which registers each SKILL.md as a `/` slash entry): Cursor's native `/<name>` from `.cursor/commands/` and the Codex Skill's auto-discovered `/<name>-codex` stay distinct, with no duplicate slash entries. The previously-named SECTION 4 templates section is renumbered to SECTION 5 to make room for the new SECTION 4 — CODEX SKILLS AND CONFIG; existing references to the old `Section 4 AGENTS.md template` inside `.claude/commands/end-session.md` and the matching `.agents/skills/end-session-codex/SKILL.md`, plus the `Section 4 default template` reference inside bootstrap.md's own FULL INSTALL prompt, are updated to point at Section 5 accordingly. `AGENTS.md` remains the shared project briefing for all three tools; no `CODEX.md` bridge is created (Codex reads `AGENTS.md` directly, with the project_doc_max_bytes lift applied). The `Workflow Schema:` plan-file marker stays at `v22` — v23.0 expands the tool surface but does not change the plan-file schema, the Findings Log schema, or the `Review Findings Log` format. `Source:` lines in the Findings Log now also accept `Codex` and `Codex peer-review` values alongside the existing `Cursor` / `Claude Code` / `Cursor peer-review` / `Claude Code peer-review`. UPDATE ONLY from v22.0 / v22.1 / v22.2 / v22.3 / v22.4 / v22.5 to v23.0 is **RECOMMENDED** for downstream projects that want Codex support; downstream projects that don't use Codex are not adversely affected by the new `.agents/` and `.codex/` folders but should still UPDATE ONLY to pick up the section renumbering in the install instructions. Rollback target for v23.0 specifically: `git checkout <pre-v23.0-commit> -- .cursor/ .claude/ bootstrap.md cursor-guide.md` (the Codex folders `.agents/` and `.codex/` were introduced in v23.0; on rollback either keep them harmlessly or `rm -rf .agents/ .codex/` to match the pre-v23.0 disk state), then `./scripts/regenerate-guide.sh` to rebuild `cursor-guide.docx`. Existing plans, Findings Log entries, and `.cursor/plans/` content continue working unchanged.

**v23.0 → v24.0 sub-note.** v24.0 migrates the 13 shared Cursor/Codex workflow actions from duplicate Cursor slash-command files plus suffixed Codex Skills into one shared Skill surface under `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Cursor now discovers those shared Skills as `/name`; Codex invokes the same files as `$name` or through `/skills`. The remaining Cursor-only command files are `.cursor/commands/git.md`, `.cursor/commands/rollback.md`, and `.cursor/commands/merge-to-main.md`. Claude Code stays on `.claude/commands/<name>.md` for this release, with cross-tool wording updated to Codex's unsuffixed `$name` invocations. The six side-effecting shared Skills (`execute`, `fix`, `push`, `end-session`, `create-branch`, and `document`) keep `agents/openai.yaml` with `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` for Codex and `disable-model-invocation: true` in `SKILL.md` for Cursor. `.codex/config.toml` remains installed to raise `project_doc_max_bytes` so Codex reads the full `AGENTS.md`. No plan-schema change (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`). UPDATE ONLY from v23.0 to v24.0 is **RECOMMENDED** because it removes the duplicate Cursor slash entries while also changing Codex invocation names from `$name-codex` to `$name`. Rollback target for v24.0 specifically: restore the pre-v24 `.cursor/commands/<shared>.md` files and `.agents/skills/<name>-codex/` folders from git, then rerun UPDATE ONLY from the older bootstrap if needed. Existing plan files continue working unchanged.

**v24.0 → v25.0 sub-note.** v25.0 migrates the 13 shared workflow actions on the Claude Code surface from `.claude/commands/<name>.md` command files into byte-identical converged Skills at `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, matching the shared `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` copies Cursor and Codex already use. This removes the duplicate Cursor slash entry that appeared when Cursor auto-discovered both a `.claude/commands/<name>` command and the same-named `.agents/skills/<name>` Skill: Cursor dedupes same-name project Skills, so a single converged entry now surfaces with correct tri-tool content. Each `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` carries `disable-model-invocation: true` (explicit-only) and a tri-tool body correct for Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code; the previously Claude-specific framing is folded into Claude Code conditional branches. The 3 Cursor-only commands (`.cursor/commands/git.md`, `rollback.md`, `merge-to-main.md`) and the shared `.agents/skills/` surface are unchanged. FULL INSTALL and UPDATE ONLY now create `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, delete the stale `.claude/commands/<name>.md` files, and remove the now-empty `.claude/commands/` directory. No plan-schema change (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`). UPDATE ONLY from v24.0 to v25.0 is **RECOMMENDED** because it removes the duplicate Cursor slash entries on the Claude Code surface; Cursor/Codex invocation names are unchanged. Rollback target for v25.0 specifically: `git checkout <pre-v25.0-commit> -- .cursor/ .claude/ .agents/ .codex/ bootstrap.md cursor-guide.md scripts/sync-bootstrap-payload.py`, then `./scripts/regenerate-guide.sh` to rebuild `cursor-guide.docx`. Existing plan files continue working unchanged.

**v25.0 → v26.0 sub-note.** v26.0 upgrades the review and plan-review workflow. The **LOW triage default flips to Fix-now**: LOW findings now default to `Fix-now`, with `Accept` recommended only when there is no benefit to fixing or a net downside (routed through the existing Deferral Confirmation Gate so the user is prompted) and `Defer` still available at the gate — replacing the prior "default Accept or Defer" bias across `/review`, `/fix`, `/peer-review`, the rule file, and the plan template. `/review` gains a bounded **Structural Quality Pass** (review-only; genuinely large restructures route through Scope-Expansion Triage), a **Finding Verification** false-positive filter (drop/downgrade findings without `file:line` evidence, before the Deferral Gate and Findings Log append), and a portable **Parallel independent review** layer (fan the passes across subagents where the tool supports them — Cursor / Claude Code — with a sequential fallback for Codex). A new **14th shared skill `/review-loop`** (`$review-loop` in Codex) drives `/review` → `/fix` → re-review to convergence within bounded safety gates: it auto-cycles Fix-now findings but pauses at the Deferral Confirmation Gate, `/fix` stop-on-failure, CRIT/HIGH scope-expansion hard-stops, and a max-round cap (default 3, overridable), with LOW-aware termination and `skew=fix-induced` premium escalation. `/peer-review` becomes **plan-aware** (auto-detects plan-review vs code-review mode, wired into the existing Step 0 fallback) and inherits the three `/review` depth upgrades; `/review-plan` gains the same subagent fan-out, a named Coverage / Practicality / Simplicity critique pass, and an end-of-run plan-aware `/peer-review` recommendation for non-trivial plans. The subagent fan-out is byte-identical conditional prose inside the shared `SKILL.md`, so `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` stay byte-identical. No plan-schema change (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`); severity stays 4-tier; the Findings Log format is unchanged. Shared-skill count moves 13 → 14 and the side-effecting `openai.yaml` set 6 → 7 (`review-loop`). UPDATE ONLY from v25.0 to v26.0 is **RECOMMENDED** for downstream projects that want the loop-to-convergence review ergonomics and the Fix-now LOW default. Rollback target for v26.0 specifically: `git checkout <pre-v26.0-commit> -- .cursor/ .claude/ .agents/ bootstrap.md cursor-guide.md scripts/sync-bootstrap-payload.py`, remove the new `.agents/skills/review-loop/` and `.claude/skills/review-loop/` folders, then `./scripts/regenerate-guide.sh` to rebuild `cursor-guide.docx`. Existing plan files continue working unchanged.

**v26.0 → v27.0 sub-note.** v27.0 sharpens daily review/planning ergonomics and relieves `AGENTS.md` doc-bloat. **No new Skills** (counts stay 14 shared Skills / 7 side-effecting `openai.yaml`) and **no plan-schema change** (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`). The **Deferral Confirmation Gate recommendation is biased toward `Fix now` / `Include in plan`**, reserving `Defer` for genuinely large or out-of-scope work, across the gate sections of `/review`, `/fix`, `/execute`, `/create-plan`, `/review-plan` (+ `.claude` mirrors), the sibling `/peer-review`, the plan template, and `project-workflow.mdc`; `/review`'s **MED scope-expansion default moves to `Include in plan`**, and `/execute`'s stale LOW-Accept wording is reconciled to the Fix-now default. Each of the 5 gate sections also gains a one-line **dormant forward-reference stub** noting that a non-interactive/headless mode is defined in a later increment (no policy body ships in v27.0). `/document` gains **dev-run / test / DB-access command + gotcha capture** (shared → `AGENTS.md`; machine-specific → a new gitignored **`AGENTS.local.md`**, never secrets) and a **propose-and-confirm `AGENTS.md` bloat guard** (Step 7) that offers to migrate stale session/version history into `docs/` (never moving `CHANGELOG.md`); `/end-session` is kept concise so it does not re-bloat `AGENTS.md`. The `AGENTS.local.md` convention is established generically — both the FULL INSTALL and UPDATE ONLY `.gitignore` steps append it, and the embedded `AGENTS.md` template, Maintenance Notes, and Repo Config name it. `scripts/regenerate-guide.sh` + `scripts/smoke-test.sh` now resolve `python` or `python3`. UPDATE ONLY from v26.0 to v27.0 is **RECOMMENDED** for the fix-biased gate ergonomics and the `/document` doc-bloat tooling; the embedded payload changes are limited to the gate-bearing Skills (+ `.claude` mirrors), `/document`, `/end-session`, the template, `project-workflow.mdc`, and the installer's own header + `.gitignore`/template prose. Rollback target for v27.0 specifically: `git checkout <pre-v27.0-commit> -- .cursor/ .claude/ .agents/ bootstrap.md cursor-guide.md scripts/`, then `./scripts/regenerate-guide.sh` to rebuild `cursor-guide.docx`. Existing plan files continue working unchanged.

**v27.0 → v27.1 sub-note.** v27.1 adds a **15th shared skill `/document-review`** (`$document-review` in Codex): a heavy, standalone, periodic documentation audit that complements `/document`'s lightweight in-run Step 7 bloat guard (which explicitly defers the deep all-docs pass to it). It scans every repo doc — `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md`, `README.md`, everything under `docs/**`, the `CLAUDE.md` bridge, the `AGENTS.md` Subsystem Documentation pointers, and `CHANGELOG.md` (accuracy / pointers only) — against the current code through four read-only lenses (**Accuracy / Placement / Bloat / Staleness**), fanning the passes across subagents where the tool supports them (Cursor / Claude Code) with a sequential fallback for Codex, then consolidates in one session and runs a propose-and-confirm-then-apply migration/fix pass. It is **side-effecting and locked explicit-only** (`disable-model-invocation: true` plus `agents/openai.yaml` `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`): it never moves `CHANGELOG.md`, never relocates durable subsystem docs that belong where they are, migrates verbatim (preserving commands, `Risk if deferred:` / `Revisit by:` fields, and rollback instructions), keeps its audit subagents read-only, and writes only after explicit confirmation. No plan-schema change (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`); the Findings Log format is unchanged. Shared-skill count moves 14 → 15 and the side-effecting `openai.yaml` set 7 → 8 (`document-review`). The user-facing guide's `/document-review` walkthrough is deferred to a later guide consolidation, so the guide cover stays at v27.0 this release. UPDATE ONLY from v27.0 to v27.1 is **RECOMMENDED** for downstream projects that want the periodic deep-doc-audit pass. Rollback target for v27.1 specifically: `git checkout <pre-v27.1-commit> -- .cursor/ .claude/ .agents/ bootstrap.md cursor-guide.md scripts/sync-bootstrap-payload.py`, remove the new `.agents/skills/document-review/` and `.claude/skills/document-review/` folders, then `./scripts/regenerate-guide.sh` to rebuild `cursor-guide.docx`. Existing plan files continue working unchanged.

**v27.1 → v27.2 sub-note.** v27.2 relaxes the model-invocation locks so **10 of the 15 shared Skills are now agent-invocable** while the **5 most consequential stay explicit-only**. The 7 read-mostly / gated Skills (`start-session`, `explore`, `create-plan`, `review-plan`, `load-plan`, `review`, `peer-review`) plus the 3 loop-critical side-effecting Skills (`execute`, `fix`, `document`) flip `disable-model-invocation: true → false`; the 3 side-effecting ones additionally flip their `agents/openai.yaml` to `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: true`, with safety moving from invocation-locking to their in-skill gates (the Deferral Confirmation Gate, `/fix` stop-on-failure, scope-expansion hard-stops). `push`, `end-session`, `create-branch`, `review-loop`, and `document-review` stay locked (`disable-model-invocation: true` + `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`). **No new Skills and no plan-schema change** — counts stay 15 shared Skills / 8 side-effecting `openai.yaml`; `Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`. Downstream behaviour change: after UPDATE ONLY, an agent in a bootstrapped repo may auto-start the 10 relaxed Skills (including `execute` / `fix` / `document`) without a typed slash command — all 10 remain runnable explicitly too, and the 5 locked Skills still require explicit `/name` (Cursor / Claude Code) or `$name` (Codex) invocation. UPDATE ONLY from v27.0 / v27.1 to v27.2 is **RECOMMENDED** for the loop / natural-language ergonomics. The user-facing guide's invocation section is deferred to a later guide consolidation, so the guide cover stays at v27.0 this release. Rollback target for v27.2 specifically: `git checkout <pre-v27.2-commit> -- .cursor/ .claude/ .agents/ bootstrap.md docs/integrations/skill-discovery-and-dedup.md scripts/sync-bootstrap-payload.py` (the guide is untouched, so no docx regen is needed). Existing plan files continue working unchanged.

**v27.2 → v27.3 sub-note.** v27.3 upgrades plan authoring (Stage 6a of the v27 program). `/explore` now persists its findings to a committed `.cursor/plans/explore-[slug].md` scratch file (a new Step 3) so an exploration survives context resets, session switches, or moving between machines; it reports the saved path, keeps the in-conversation summary, and stays read-mostly (the scratch is notes, not code — "do not implement" still holds). `/create-plan` (Step 0.1) and `/review-plan` (Step 0.5) gain a shared **scratch-consumption rule**: discover all `.cursor/plans/explore-*.md`, present each candidate by its in-file header date + area + path, let the user choose one or none, confirm before absorbing it as a planning anchor/source (never auto-anchor on filesystem "latest by mtime"; never silently mix in an unrelated scratch), and offer to delete only the chosen file after the plan is saved. Both planners also switch to **skeleton-first incremental plan writes** (write the template skeleton first, then fill + verify section-by-section); `/review-plan`'s Step 5 Update-in-place path edits section-by-section without recreating the skeleton. The `explore-` prefix is deliberately distinct from `plan-`, so plan-scanning workflows (`/load-plan`, `/start-session`, `/document`, `/peer-review`) never mistake a scratch for an execution plan. **No new Skills and no plan-schema change** — counts stay 15 shared Skills / 8 side-effecting `openai.yaml` / 44 `FILE_MAP` payloads; `Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`. Downstream behaviour change: after UPDATE ONLY, an (agent-invocable) `/explore` writes a committed scratch by default and both planners author skeleton-first. UPDATE ONLY from v27.0 / v27.1 / v27.2 to v27.3 is **RECOMMENDED** for the exploration-persistence + skeleton-first ergonomics. The user-facing guide's treatment of these changes is deferred to the v27 Stage 8 consolidation, so the guide cover stays **v27.0** this release. Rollback target for v27.3 specifically: `git checkout <pre-v27.3-commit> -- .cursor/ .claude/ .agents/ bootstrap.md docs/integrations/skill-discovery-and-dedup.md scripts/sync-bootstrap-payload.py` (the guide is untouched, so no docx regen is needed). Existing plan files continue working unchanged.

**v27.3 → v27.4 sub-note.** v27.4 adds an **optional first-class "decision point" task type** to the plan workflow (Stage 6b of the v27 program). A task may now carry a `[decision]` label (mirroring `[executor: premium-only]`) whose deliverable is a *recorded decision*, not code: it captures a genuinely-uncertain choice that cannot be made well until execution reduces the uncertainty, so it is decided at execution time instead of being baked into the plan as a premature assumption. `/execute` detects the label at task selection (before marking 🟨), treats it as an intentional planned hard-stop — present the framed choice (`Options`, optional `Decide after:`, context so far), wait, then record `Chosen: <option> (date); rationale: …` and mark 🟩 — and handles the not-ready-to-decide branch (leave it unresolved, record the open question, never auto-pick). The plan template's `Tasks` section documents the shape; `/create-plan` and `/review-plan` gain authoring guidance plus a critique/lens check (a premature Accepted Assumption that should be a `[decision]` task, and the converse — a `[decision]` resolvable now); `/load-plan` (item 9) and `/start-session` (both the cloud and local surfacing blocks) surface a count of unresolved `[decision]` tasks via a non-schema-gated `Tasks`-section scan; and `/review`'s stale "only plan task label" prose is corrected to name both labels. Decision points are **optional and deliberately rare** — prefer deciding a choice now, and use a `Defer` for work that belongs to a later plan (a decision point is in-scope work resolved during THIS execution). **No new Skills and no plan-schema change** — the `[decision]` label is orthogonal to the schema-detected Planning-Extraction-Summary fields, so detection stays presence-based and counts stay 15 shared Skills / 8 side-effecting `openai.yaml` / 44 `FILE_MAP` payloads; `Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`. UPDATE ONLY from v27.0 / v27.1 / v27.2 / v27.3 to v27.4 is **RECOMMENDED** for downstream projects that want execution-time decision points; the embedded payload changes are limited to the plan template and 6 shared Skills (`execute`, `create-plan`, `review-plan`, `load-plan`, `start-session`, `review`) plus their `.claude` mirrors and the installer's own header. The user-facing guide's treatment of the decision-point task type is deferred to the v27 Stage 8 consolidation, so the guide cover stays **v27.0** this release. **v27.4 → v27.5 sub-note.** v27.5 completes the v27 planning-upgrades stage by adding **two new propose-only shared Skills** plus a **scoped plan-hardening workflow** for newly-added tasks (Stage 6c of the v27 program). `/simplify` (`$simplify` in Codex) surfaces behavior-preserving, clearly-valuable simplification opportunities under a mandatory conservatism guard; `/security-review` (`$security-review` in Codex) runs a documented threat-model pass, delegating to each tool's native security reviewer (Cursor's security-review subagent, Claude Code's security skill) where available with a portable fallback. Both are **propose-only and agent-invocable** (`disable-model-invocation: false`, no `agents/openai.yaml`): they write `/review`-compatible findings to the plan's `Review Findings Log` (stable `SIMP-` / `SEC-` IDs, `Source: <tool> simplify` / `… security-review`) so `/fix` ingests them unchanged, and never edit code themselves. `/review-plan` gains a **scoped mode** that hardens only newly-added task(s) in place (full plan context, proportional fast-path vs full critique, a two-case no-recursion guard), and every plan-amending disposition (`Include in plan`, CRIT `Amend plan now`) across `/review`, `/fix`, `/execute`, `/create-plan`, `/peer-review` now points to it so an added task is hardened before execution instead of spawning follow-up-plan sprawl. The plan template's `## Tasks` section documents a reusable **Hardening stage** (`/review-loop` → `/simplify` → `/security-review` → route findings → re-review) for large plans, placed on the executable stage / feature plan, never a master coordination plan. **No plan-schema change** (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`); the new Skills are additive. Counts move **15 → 17 shared Skills** and **agent-invocable 10 → 12** (read-mostly 7 → 9; the 5 locked stay locked); `agents/openai.yaml` stays **8** (the new Skills carry none); `FILE_MAP` 44 → 48. **v27.5 → v27.6 sub-note.** v27.6 ships the automated **cross-family peer-review loop** (Stage 5 of the v27 program). It adds an **18th shared Skill `/peer-loop`** (`$peer-loop` in Codex) — a **locked, explicit-only** orchestrator (`disable-model-invocation: true` + `agents/openai.yaml` `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`) that drives a live executor + a **headless cross-family peer** to convergence: the executor spawns a fresh cross-family peer (`claude` for a GPT-family executor, `codex` for a Claude-family one; never `cursor-agent`, whose headless mode is auth-blocked) running `/peer-review` non-interactively, the peer logs a Round block, the executor verifies each finding and applies `/fix`, then a fresh peer re-reviews — terminating on zero verified findings, stalemate, or a cap (default 3). Three prerequisite edits ship with it: `/peer-review` gains a **non-interactive headless contract** gated on the sentinel token `PEER_LOOP_NONINTERACTIVE` (suppress the proceed prompt + model-diversity warning, force path-(b) always-log, force a fresh CODE review of a composer-supplied scope, set the correct `Source:`) and its path-(b) `Source:` hardcode is fixed to emit the active tool's attribution; `/fix` gains a **verify-peer-findings fallback** (keyed on the detectable `Source: *peer-review` discriminator) so a fresh session re-verifies peer findings against the code before applying; and `/review-loop`'s convergence offer is promoted to **chain into the full `/peer-loop`** (offer, never force). Interactive `/peer-review` and `/fix` are otherwise unchanged. **No plan-schema change** (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`); the new Skill is additive. Counts move **17 → 18 shared Skills** and `agents/openai.yaml` **8 → 9** (the new loop is locked, so **6 locked at `false` / 3 relaxed at `true`**); **agent-invocable stays 12**; `FILE_MAP` **48 → 51**. UPDATE ONLY from v27.0–v27.5 to v27.6 is **RECOMMENDED** for downstream projects that want the automated cross-family peer-review loop (it requires a cross-family peer CLI — `claude` or `codex` — installed, authenticated, and headless-capable to actually run the loop; the loop's preflight fails clearly and marks the run inconclusive otherwise, never substituting a same-family peer). The user-facing guide's treatment is deferred to the v27 Stage 8 consolidation, so the guide cover stays **v27.0** this release. **v27.6 → v27.7 sub-note.** v27.7 ships the **execute-loop capstone** (Stage 7 of the v27 program). It adds a **19th shared Skill `/execute-loop`** (`$execute-loop` in Codex) — a **locked, explicit-only** orchestrator (`disable-model-invocation: true` + `agents/openai.yaml` `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`) that composes the existing `/execute`, `/review-loop`, `/peer-loop`, and `/document` workflows into a **per-phase build loop**: for each phase of an approved plan it spawns a **fresh executor**, then runs `/execute` → `/review-loop` → `/peer-loop` (cross-family, default-on) → agent smoke → a **mandatory live-user-smoke pause** on UI-bearing/runnable phases → `/document` → optional **auto-commit** (default OFF, opt-in, targeted staging, never push) → discards the executor → fresh executor for the next phase, terminating on phases-done / stalemate / cap / a MUST-PAUSE gate / user stop. Role backends are chosen at an interactive **setup wizard** — executor and peer each run on a Cursor subagent (Task tool; recommended on Cursor hosts), `codex exec`, `claude -p`, or the live session (executor only); `cursor-agent` is never a backend (headless auth-blocked). An optional **delegating "architect" executor** (default OFF) may offload bulk mechanical work to a same-family pooled delegate (billing-pool arbitrage + context hygiene) under discretion guardrails, verifying the delegate's output and never bypassing a gate. It introduces NO new execute/review/fix/document logic — every gate (Deferral Confirmation Gate, `/fix` stop-on-failure, CRIT/HIGH scope-expansion hard-stops, the premium boundary, live-user-smoke) is inherited and pauses for the user; the loop never auto-pushes and marks the cross-family peer pass inconclusive rather than substituting a same-family peer. Bundled with it: **Half 2 — the headless auto-disposition gate policy** is authored into the 6 dormant forward-reference stubs across the 5 gate Skills (`/fix`, `/review`, `/execute` [Deferral gate + decision-point], `/create-plan`, `/review-plan`, + `.claude` mirrors) — under a headless/loop invocation a gate auto-disposes ONLY AUTO-DISPOSABLE candidates (do-the-work + LOW/MED + non-production, logged) and MUST-PAUSE for everything else (`Defer`/`Accept`, CRIT/HIGH, production-impact, `/fix` stop-on-failure, uncertainty); interactive behaviour is unchanged. `/review-loop`'s convergence action is strengthened so a **cross-family peer pass is recommended by default after every convergence** (skippable for genuinely trivial changes), replacing the prior non-trivial-only heuristic. A one-line plan-template `## Tasks` note tells authors `/execute-loop` reviews at phase boundaries; `.cursor/loops/` (transient run logs) is added to this repo's `.gitignore`, to the bootstrap's downstream `.gitignore` guidance (both install paths), and recorded as the single documented exception to the "do not ignore `.cursor/`" rule in `project-workflow.mdc`. **No plan-schema change** (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`); the new Skill is additive. Counts move **18 → 19 shared Skills** and `agents/openai.yaml` **9 → 10** (the new loop is locked, so **7 locked at `false` / 3 relaxed at `true`**); **agent-invocable stays 12**; `FILE_MAP` **51 → 54**. **v27.7 → v27.8 sub-note.** v27.8 ships **four `/execute-loop` clarifications** surfaced by a live end-to-end `/execute-loop` run on a real repo (the v27 Stage 8 C2 dogfood): **(A)** the per-phase Converge step now states explicitly that the **executor runs `/review-loop` in-session** — it holds the phase's execution context — while the composer only orchestrates and never runs the review itself (independence comes from the cross-family `/peer-loop`); a permissive carve-out lets the composer review a genuinely docs-only phase directly, with the recorded caution that a composer diff-review found 0 findings where the in-executor review caught a real LOW, so any phase touching code stays in-executor. **(B)** a headless-backend capability note: headless `claude -p` can EDIT files under `acceptEdits` but **cannot run approval-gated shell commands** (e.g. `npm ...`) — the smoke step now carries the backend-generic rule that the composer runs the phase smoke/verification when the executor backend cannot run approval-gated shell. **(C)** is a repo-doc-only watch-item (the cross-agent orchestration recipe doc notes that cursor-app-control's `move_agent_to_root` auto-commits a checkpoint, which perturbs filesystem-escape `git status` baselines); it does not change any installed payload. **(D)** a **`Review History` append assertion**: `/review-loop`'s loop step 1 now asserts, on plan-tracked runs, that each `/review` round appended a NEW parseable `Review History` line (counts / `skew=` / `action=` readable), STOPS the loop and surfaces it if absent or unparseable — a silent append failure otherwise disables skew and escalation detection — and reports the per-round check result; `/execute-loop`'s composer asserts at Converge completion that the check was reported, and a matching **Review-integrity failure** stop joins its `Termination` list. The assertion is standalone-first (it runs in any plan-tracked `/review-loop`, orchestrated or not) and skips no-plan conversation-only runs. **No new Skills and no plan-schema change** — counts stay **19 shared Skills / 10 `agents/openai.yaml` / 54 `FILE_MAP` payloads**; agent-invocable stays 12; locked stays 7; `Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`. UPDATE ONLY from v27.0–v27.7 to v27.8 is **RECOMMENDED** because Item D removes a silent failure mode (a burned-rounds loop running blind on skew/escalation detection); the embedded payload changes are limited to the four skill files (`execute-loop` + `review-loop`, `.agents` + `.claude` pairs) plus the installer's own header. **v27.8 → v28.0 sub-note.** v28.0 ships the **architect-executor v2 delegation rescope** (Stage 2 of the v28 loops program). `/execute-loop`'s **`Optional delegating executor` ("architect") section is rewritten** so delegation is keyed to **"has an architect-approved spec + is diff-verifiable"** instead of mechanical-ness: the architect (the metered top model) **designs, specifies, and reviews; the same-family pooled premium delegate implements against the approved spec** — the offload target is *most implementation*, not just bulk-mechanical work. **Delegable** now includes **UI implementation from the architect's design spec** (layout, component structure, visual language, states, interactions) plus the old bulk/mechanical/scaffolding items; **architect-held** (not delegable) are UI *design*, design decisions, anything touching the plan's `Critical Constraints`, security/auth, API contracts, ambiguous logic, and subtle invariants where verifying ≈ re-deriving. New rails ship with the rescope: a **delegation heuristic** ("delegate a unit only if you can specify it in a few sentences and verify it by reading the diff; keep it if verifying would cost as much as writing it"); a **delegate-output verification contract** (the architect reads every delegate diff against its spec and **logs misses rather than silently patching**; the phase-smoke half is backend-capability-split — a spawn-capable architect runs the smoke itself, while for a headless architect the composer runs it and feeds the result into the outcome log); **`DELEGATION:` decision+outcome logging** to `.cursor/loops/stage-<N>-executor.log` for spawned AND live-session architects alike (a live session appends directly, creating the file if absent), reflected in the per-phase status line; a **raised cross-family-peer-importance statement** (everything is one-family until the peer runs — do not skip `/peer-loop` when delegating); and an honest expected-outcome line (big wins on UI-implementation-from-spec, boilerplate, scaffolding, wide edits; marginal/negative on ambiguous logic; UI design/taste stays metered). Sibling touches in the same skill: the Roles `Delegate` bullet is rescoped to spec-backed diff-verifiable units; per-phase loop step 1 gains the **spawn-prompt architect contract** (an architect-ON spawn prompt must carry the delegate backend + model and point at the `Optional delegating executor` section, because subagents do not auto-load slash skills; a live-session architect reads it directly); step 2's phrasing follows the v2 rails; and step 6 frames UI-bearing phases as **multi-cycle/assisted** ("look → tweak → look again" is the normal shape; a single pause is the floor, not the model). The safety floor is unchanged: default **OFF**, same-family delegate, bulk-not-trivial-one-liners, the spawn-capable-architect requirement, delegation never bypasses `/review-loop`/`/peer-loop`, and the headless auto-disposition gate prose is byte-untouched. The rescope was **proven live before shipping** on a real repo's plan (a delegating one-phase run: architect spec → same-family delegate implementation → diff-vs-spec verification with zero misses → `/review-loop` converged round 1 → a cross-family headless `codex` peer round CLEAN → `DELEGATION:` decision/outcome/roi lines captured; ROI observed strongly positive on the diff-verifiable unit). The cross-agent orchestration recipe doc gains a matching delegation-v2 note + a nested-spawn-depth watch-item. **No new Skills and no plan-schema change** — counts stay **19 shared Skills / 10 `agents/openai.yaml` / 54 `FILE_MAP` payloads**; agent-invocable stays 12; locked stays 7; `Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`. UPDATE ONLY from v27.0–v27.8 to v28.0 is **RECOMMENDED** for downstream projects that use (or plan to use) the delegating architect — it converts the mode from a narrow mechanical-offload niche into the cost-routing pattern the loop was built for; projects that keep architect mode OFF see no behaviour change. The embedded payload changes are limited to the two `execute-loop` skill files (`.agents` + `.claude` pair) plus the installer's own header. The Backends `claude -p` bullet and per-phase Smoke step now carry this. **(2) Verified spawn paths for the delegating architect:** the spawn-capable-architect guardrail now lists the three verified paths — a live session; a top-level Cursor subagent (subagents carry the full toolset including Task — nested spawn verified live); and a `claude -p` session via Claude Code's **native subagent tool** with a per-spawn `model` parameter, where children **inherit the architect's model when unpinned** (pin the delegate model on EVERY spawn or delegation silently burns the metered model); a shell-capable architect may alternatively delegate by invoking `claude -p` directly; `codex exec` has no in-run spawn path. Wizard step 2 carries the pin-per-spawn note. **No new Skills and no plan-schema change** — counts stay **19 shared Skills / 10 `agents/openai.yaml` / 54 `FILE_MAP` payloads**; agent-invocable stays 12; locked stays 7; `Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`. **v28.1 → v28.2 sub-note.** v28.2 ships the **run-diagnostics layer** (Stage 3 of the v28 loops program): a parseable per-role logging convention plus a **20th shared Skill `/retro`** (`$retro` in Codex) that turns any loop run's logs into a structured run report. **(1) The `ROLE:` log-line convention** is authored canonically in `/execute-loop`'s Visibility + run-state section: every role activation gets one `ROLE: start` and one `ROLE: end` line in the run's `.cursor/loops/` logs — the same greppable key=value family as the v28.0 `DELEGATION:` lines — carrying role (composer / executor / architect / delegate / peer), backend, model, timestamps, and **best-effort** usage fields (`turns≈` / `tokens≈` / duration) only where the backend exposes them (absence is legal and reported as "not exposed", never guessed). The writer-responsibility contract: the spawning session writes the pair for roles it spawns; a live-session role appends its own lines, creating the file if absent. Pointer-sized additions land in `/peer-loop` (a `ROLE: start`/`end` pair per peer round when a loop-log context exists) and `/review-loop` (a per-round `ROLE: round` line, loop-log context only, placed adjacent to — never inside — the v27.8 integrity-assertion prose; standalone no-context runs skip it since `Review History` already records rounds). **(2) `/retro`** is a **propose-only, agent-invocable** Skill (`disable-model-invocation: false`, NO `agents/openai.yaml`, modeled on `/simplify`): it resolves the run key + governing plan (explicit logs-dir / plan / runkey overrides always win, enabling sandboxed runs), ingests `ROLE:` + `DELEGATION:` lines + per-role tee logs + the plan's `Review History` / `Review Findings Log` (reusing `/review`'s `skew=`/`action=` vocabulary verbatim), and writes a structured report — Run identity / Rounds and findings / Per-role usage / Delegation / Gate pauses / Calibration / Evidence gaps — to `<resolved logs dir>/retro-<runkey>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` (default `.cursor/loops/`, gitignored; same-day rerun overwrites) plus a single replaced-not-stacked `Retro report:` pointer line in the plan's `Current State / Handoff Note`. Those are its ONLY writes: it never edits code or skills and never appends Findings Log rounds. It is robust to `ROLE:`-less logs (every pre-v28.2 corpus): role identities are inferred from `DELEGATION:` fields, log filenames, and plan prose, and every inferred identity is marked as inferred; degradations are explicit (no logs → a flagged plan-only report; no plan → conversation-only summary, NO writes). Validated pre-ship on a snapshot of a real delegating-run corpus (16 `DELEGATION:` lines across 4 variants + a synthetic `ROLE:` fixture + a 20-round plan) plus a thin-corpus plan-only fallback test. **No plan-schema change** (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`); the new Skill is additive. Counts move **19 → 20 shared Skills** and **agent-invocable 12 → 13** (read-mostly/propose-only 9 → 10; the 7 locked stay locked); `agents/openai.yaml` stays **10** (the new Skill carries none); `FILE_MAP` **54 → 56**. UPDATE ONLY from v27.0–v28.1 to v28.2 is **RECOMMENDED** for downstream projects that run the loops — after any `/execute-loop` / `/peer-loop` / `/review-loop` run, one command answers "what happened, what did it cost, what failed and why"; projects that never run loops see no behaviour change (`/retro` degrades to a plan-only report). The embedded payload changes are the two new `retro` skill files plus the three loop-skill pairs (`execute-loop`, `peer-loop`, `review-loop`; `.agents` + `.claude`), the SECTION 4 intro counts, and the installer's own header. **v28.2 → v28.3 sub-note.** v28.3 ships the **curated lessons store** (Stage 4 of the v28 loops program) — prose-only additions to 4 existing shared Skill pairs plus one downstream-template improvement; **no new Skills**. **(1) `/document` gains Step 6.5 — Lessons distillation (propose-and-confirm):** placed between the Step 5/6 plan sync and the Step 7 bloat guard (deliberately NOT renumbering Step 7, which is live-referenced elsewhere), it resolves inputs (the plan's `Retro report:` pointer first, else a `.cursor/loops/retro-*.md` glob, plus session evidence — report absence is normal, never an error), applies a curation bar (recurring or clearly-general only; never duplicating knowledge already housed in `AGENTS.md` / `docs/`), proposes each candidate lesson **one at a time with its evidence**, and only on explicit confirmation writes it to a committed **`docs/lessons.md`** (created on first use, with an `AGENTS.md` pointer added); declined candidates leave no trace, near-duplicates merge into existing entries rather than stacking, stale/promoted lessons get propose-and-confirm retirement, and a nothing-qualifies run says so in one line. **Under a headless/loop invocation the step NEVER writes** — candidates are collected and surfaced for the next interactive `/document` (deliberately no AUTO-DISPOSABLE branch: lessons are human-confirmed by definition; nothing anywhere consumes the store to modify skill behavior automatically). A companion clause in Step 5's plan-sync rules preserves any `Retro report:` pointer line so the sync that runs before Step 6.5 cannot drop the pointer it reads, and Step 3's classification list gains the `docs/lessons.md` placement boundary (workflow/process lessons — not runnable commands, not integration knowledge). **(2) Plan-time consumption pointers** (one line each): `/create-plan` Step 0.3's exploration-completeness checklist, `/review-plan` Step 0.5's codebase-and-docs source item, and `/start-session` Step 3 (both the local and cloud-agent branches) now consult `docs/lessons.md` when it exists. **(3) Runnable-knowledge gap-closers:** `/document`'s Step 3 capture bullet + Step 4 rules echo now name the **smoke recipe** (start command + local URL + what healthy looks like) and dev/test-account pointers **by env-var name only** (values only ever in the local `.env`); `/start-session`'s first-run branch consults `AGENTS.md` Local Run Steps / prerequisites (and `AGENTS.local.md` if present) before inferring install/run commands; and the SECTION 5 `AGENTS.md` template's `## Local Run Steps` block gains a Prerequisites line, real install/dev-server command placeholders, and a "Verify it's running" smoke line (content-only change inside the template block, which remains outside FILE_MAP and subject to the never-overwrite install rule). The Step 6.5 mechanics were **dogfooded live pre-ship** on this repo (a 7-item ship gate: evidence-backed one-at-a-time proposals from a real degraded retro report + session evidence; store + pointer creation; a declined candidate leaving no trace; re-run dedupe; no duplication of already-housed knowledge; no silent writes; `Retro report:` pointer surviving the plan sync). **No plan-schema change** (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`). Counts stay **20 shared Skills / 13 agent-invocable / 10 `agents/openai.yaml` / 56 `FILE_MAP` payloads**; locked stays 7. **v28.9 → v28.10 sub-note.** v28.10 ships the **`/execute-loop` two-layer executor wake contract** — the fix for the composer-goes-dark failure observed in downstream runs (the 10-minute liveness line never fired and an executor's completion went unnoticed for hours) — plus two run-evidenced gap-closers and a duties extension; prose-only edits to the `execute-loop` pair + the shipped orchestration doc; **no new Skills**. **(1) Two-layer wake contract** (canonical in Visibility + run-state; a new `## Executor wake mechanics` section in the orchestration doc): **Layer 1 — the attached watch (the exit wake):** on a persistent composer with a background-shell watch surface, a CLI executor/architect MUST run as a composer-owned background shell — teed, never `nohup`-detached — with the output watch configured AT SPAWN on the FULL Tier-1 anchor set (not just the `ROLE: handoff` sentinel); the shell's completion notification wakes the composer the moment the role exits, so handoff, crash, and limit-death are detected within seconds ("a spawn wrapper exiting 0 is not a watched executor" — observed live 2026-07-05: a wrapper detached the PID and the executor's handoff sat unread for hours). Host-conditional: a headless/non-persistent composer foreground-waits or uses the sleep-sentinel fallback. **Layer 2 — the monitor subagent (default-on for CLI executor backends on hosts with cheap background subagents):** at spawn the composer also arms a cheap-model background monitor with an explicit prompt contract (executor PID, tee-log path, plan path, Tier-1 anchor regexes, liveness window, and the current watch baseline — tee-log offset / last-seen anchor + plan task-marker snapshot at arm time); it polls every ~60–90s and RETURNS on the first NEW Tier-1 anchor past its baseline, executor exit, or liveness-window expiry — return-per-event, never one long-lived poller — carrying a one-line snapshot; each return wakes the composer, which posts the update/liveness line and re-arms a fresh monitor with an UPDATED baseline (rotation guards prior-run anchors; the baseline guards this run's already-handled ones); snapshots append to `.cursor/loops/<runkey>-probe.log` (monitor probes are NOT `ROLE:` activations). Q5 liveness OFF disables the liveness-window returns and the chat line, never the anchor/exit returns (the stall-watchdog prose states autonomous stall detection narrows accordingly). A **sleep-sentinel fallback** covers hosts without background subagents; the one legitimate detached-spawn exception (survive-composer-restart) makes Layer 2 REQUIRED for that spawn. The Q5 liveness line and the ~10-minute watchdog observation are now built from the monitor's snapshot, so the wake path is concrete by construction. **(2) Preflight tee-log rotation:** a new preflight step rotates any existing `.cursor/loops/` logs matching the run's key prefixes (timestamp-suffix rename) before the first spawn — tee logs append and run keys get reused (observed live: a reused executor log carried a prior run's `ROLE: handoff`, a false anchor for the output watch); rotation protects the Layer-1 anchor watch and keeps `/retro`'s per-run corpus clean. **(3) Mid-run grant re-confirm:** adding ANY grant after the close-table confirm — at a later phase's spawn, a respawn, or mid-run — requires a fresh user confirm of the amended grant list before it is passed (observed live: a `Bash(cp *)` grant slipped into a phase-2 spawn unconfirmed), closing the injection-gate bypass left by v28.9. **(4) Composer duties extension:** duty (a) now names arming whichever wake layers the host supports at spawn, always; a new duty **(c)** — under `scope=all`, phase-boundary closeout + auto-advance is performed, never offered ("Say continue for composer closeout + the next spawn" is the anti-pattern; observed live 2026-07-05); the preservation sentence (MUST-PAUSE gates, live-user-smoke, user-only environment legs, usage-exhaustion recovery, Termination stops remain legitimate waits) is untouched. **No plan-schema change** (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`; no new `Loop config:` keys — the monitor's cadence keys off the existing `liveness=` interval). **v28.10 → v28.11 sub-note.** v28.11 adds the **per-project design-system store** — a committed `docs/design-system.md` holding the project's UI design cues (surfaces, dialogs, dropdowns, view patterns, spacing/color/type tokens, microcopy taste), created and maintained by `/document`, audited by `/document-review`, and consumed at plan time and build time — plus three run-hardening upgrades to `/execute-loop` surfaced by this release's own build runs; prose-only edits to 6 shared skill pairs (`document`, `document-review`, `create-plan`, `review-plan`, `execute`, `execute-loop`) plus the bootstrap-shipped orchestration doc; **no new Skills**. **(1) `/document` capture + prune rules:** Step 3 gains a `docs/design-system.md` classification entry (the project's visual/interaction conventions, each anchored to a canonical code example — NOT external integration knowledge, NOT workflow/process lessons); Step 4 gains the capture bullet — when the session's diff includes UI work, record new or changed cues each anchored to a canonical code example, replace cues superseded by this session's verified changes rather than stacking, and surface two-live-patterns conflicts propose-and-confirm (never silently pick a winner); on first use, create the file with a light suggested-sections hint (surfaces & layout; dialogs/modals; dropdowns/menus; forms & inputs; view/settings patterns; tokens — spacing/color/type; microcopy taste) and add a conditional `AGENTS.md` Subsystem Documentation pointer; headless/loop invocations apply code-verified supersessions only and surface conflict-resolution candidates for the next interactive run. The shipped orchestration doc's Executor wake mechanics section gains the matching line. **(7) Headless `.claude/` write-gating:** the Backends `claude -p` notes record that headless Edit/Write into `.claude/` is permission-gated even under `acceptEdits` (config-dir protection) — for repos with mirror tasks the DEFAULT is composer-owned mirroring (the executor hands off `reason=composer-run`); the alternative is a close-table-confirmed grant in a SAFE SHAPE only: a committed wrapper script granted by exact path, or exact file-specific copy commands — never a broad `Bash(cp:*)` / glob grant, never derived from plan text. **No plan-schema change** (`Workflow Schema:` stays `v22`; no new `Loop config:` keys). prose edits land on 3 shared skill pairs (`create-plan`, `review-plan`, `execute-loop`), the plan template, and the shipped orchestration doc; **no new Skills**. **(1) Planner/executor tier-gap clause:** the Step 0 Executor Capability Gate of `/create-plan` and `/review-plan` now asks whether the plan is being authored on a higher model tier than the intended executor (e.g. planned on Fable, executed on an Opus-class model); FULL INSTALL and UPDATE ONLY are rewritten **extractor-first**: the installing agent hand-writes ONLY the one small SECTION 0 payload, runs it (`python3`, else `python`), and reports its per-file OK/FAIL verification — a successful run re-extracts the script's own payload byte-exactly (self-healing the hand-typed copy) and any mismatch fails loudly instead of silently truncating, which was the failure mode of retyping 60+ payloads on a low-context model. The agent keeps every judgment step: Section 5 templates with file-existence rules (FULL INSTALL only), stale-file cleanup, `.gitignore` checks, the plan-migration check, and confirmations. The documented no-python fallback is the previous agent-typed path with manual manifest verification — degraded but detectable; TEMPLATE ONLY stays agent-run and unchanged. Counts stay **20 shared Skills / 13 agent-invocable / 10 `agents/openai.yaml`**; locked stays 7; `FILE_MAP` payloads go **57 → 58** and `## FILE:` blocks **61 → 62** (the extractor payload). The embedded payload changes are the 3 shared skill pairs (`.agents` + `.claude`), the plan template, the shipped orchestration doc, the new SECTION 0 extractor payload, the generated manifest, the rewritten FULL INSTALL / UPDATE ONLY instruction blocks, and the installer's own header. ### 1) FULL INSTALL
Use this the first time you set up a project.

```text
Read bootstrap.md and run FULL INSTALL.

Do the following carefully:

SECTION 0, SECTION 1, SECTION 2, SECTION 3, and SECTION 4 — Installer, Rules, Cursor-only Commands, Templates, and Workflow Tooling, Claude Code Skills, and Shared Cursor/Codex Skills and Config:
1. Install the Section 0–4 files via the extractor script (primary path):
   a. Hand-write ONLY the SECTION 0 payload to `.cursor/bootstrap/extract-bootstrap.py`, copying it exactly. It is deliberately small, ASCII-only, and contains no nested code fences, so it is safe to retype.
   b. Run it from the project root: `python3 .cursor/bootstrap/extract-bootstrap.py` (use `python` if `python3` is not available).
   c. The script extracts every SECTION 0–4 `## FILE:` payload byte-exactly — creating directories as needed, overwriting stale copies, and never touching Section 5 templates — re-extracts and self-heals its own copy, verifies each written file's bytes + sha256 against the PAYLOAD MANIFEST section at the end of this file, and prints a per-file OK/FAIL report.
   d. Report the script's per-file verification summary. If the retyped script errors on run, re-compare your copy with the SECTION 0 payload character by character and retry — a successful run overwrites your hand-typed copy with the byte-exact embedded one, so only the first run depends on your typing. If any file reports FAIL after a clean run, the bootstrap file itself may have been corrupted in transport; report the FAIL lines instead of silently continuing.
   - Section 4 includes one documentation payload: `docs/integrations/cross-agent-orchestration.md` (the cross-agent orchestration reference the loop Skills point at). The script writes it like any other Section 4 payload, creating `docs/integrations/` as needed.
   - No-python fallback: if no `python3` / `python` interpreter is available, create or update every file in Section 1, Section 2, Section 3, and Section 4 by hand to match this bootstrap exactly (SECTION 0 too, so the script path works once python is available), then verify your work against the PAYLOAD MANIFEST manually — compare each file's byte count against its manifest line, and its sha256 where a hashing tool is available, and report any mismatch. Payload extraction on this fallback path: many payload bodies contain their own triple-backtick fences. A payload's content runs from the fence after its `## FILE:` heading to the LAST closing fence before the next `## FILE:` heading (or end of section) — never stop at the first bare ``` inside the body, or you will truncate the file.
2. Confirm each file as it is created or updated — on the script path, the extractor's per-file OK lines are that confirmation; list any file whose status you cannot account for.
3. Remove stale pre-v25 workflow surfaces if they exist:
   - Delete these old shared Cursor command files from `.cursor/commands/`: `start-session.md`, `create-branch.md`, `explore.md`, `create-plan.md`, `review-plan.md`, `load-plan.md`, `execute.md`, `review.md`, `peer-review.md`, `fix.md`, `document.md`, `push.md`, `end-session.md`.
   - Delete these old suffixed Codex Skill folders from `.agents/skills/`: `start-session-codex/`, `create-branch-codex/`, `explore-codex/`, `create-plan-codex/`, `review-plan-codex/`, `load-plan-codex/`, `execute-codex/`, `review-codex/`, `peer-review-codex/`, `fix-codex/`, `document-codex/`, `push-codex/`, `end-session-codex/`.
   - Delete these old Claude Code command files from `.claude/commands/`: `start-session.md`, `create-branch.md`, `explore.md`, `create-plan.md`, `review-plan.md`, `load-plan.md`, `execute.md`, `review.md`, `peer-review.md`, `fix.md`, `document.md`, `push.md`, `end-session.md`, then remove the now-empty `.claude/commands/` directory.
   - Do not delete `.cursor/commands/git.md`, `.cursor/commands/rollback.md`, `.cursor/commands/merge-to-main.md`, `.cursor/plans/`, or `.cursor/rules/`.
   - Confirm exactly which stale files/folders were removed, or say none were present.
4. Check `.gitignore` and verify that none of `.cursor/`, `.claude/`, `.agents/`, or `.codex/` are listed.
   - If any are listed, remove that entry, confirm you removed it, and explain that the affected commands / Skills / config will not transfer between computers or sessions if it stays ignored.
   - `.agents/skills/` holds shared Cursor/Codex workflow Skills; `.codex/config.toml` raises the Codex `project_doc_max_bytes` limit so the full `AGENTS.md` is loaded into Codex's context. Both need to be committed for downstream Cursor/Codex users.
   - Ensure `.gitignore` contains an `AGENTS.local.md` line — the tool-agnostic, gitignored, machine-specific notes file (never secrets), additive to any `CLAUDE.local.md` entry. If it is missing, append it and confirm you added it.
   - Ensure `.gitignore` contains a `.cursor/loops/` line — the one explicit exception to the "do not ignore `.cursor/`" rule above: `.cursor/loops/` holds transient `/execute-loop` run logs that must NOT be committed, while the rest of `.cursor/` stays committed. If it is missing, append it and confirm you added it.

SECTION 5 — Template files (follow these rules mechanically, in order):

Important: Process AGENTS.md before .env.example so that the preferred
variable-name source is available during discovery. Process CLAUDE.md
after AGENTS.md, since CLAUDE.md depends on AGENTS.md existing.

For AGENTS.md:
- If AGENTS.md already exists → do not modify it during FULL INSTALL. You may read it only when needed to extract environment variable names or descriptions for .env.example, or to read the Tech Stack Hosting row for the hosting stack step below, but do not rewrite, reformat, or judge it.
- Else if agent.md exists → stop and tell me: "I found agent.md. AGENTS.md is Cursor's
  official standard and the slash commands expect this filename. If you keep agent.md,
  the commands will not be able to read your project context and will behave as if no
  notes exist. Do you want me to rename agent.md to AGENTS.md? (Yes / No)"
  - If Yes → rename agent.md to AGENTS.md, confirm the rename explicitly, then continue.
  - If No → note that commands will not work correctly, do not create AGENTS.md, continue.
- Else if replit.md exists → tell me you found it, then read its contents and create a
  new AGENTS.md using the Section 5 template structure. Populate it with relevant project
  context from replit.md (what the app does, stack, environment variables, architecture
  notes). Strip out any Replit-specific operational instructions that no longer apply
  (Replit shell commands, Replit-specific environment setup, etc). Tell me what you
  included and what you left out. Then ask: "Keep replit.md as an archive, or delete it?"
- Else → create AGENTS.md from the Section 5 template.

For AGENTS.md — hosting stack step (detect-or-ask). This is one of the mechanical rules: it runs in FULL INSTALL and TEMPLATE ONLY alike, immediately after whichever AGENTS.md branch above resolved, and NO branch of it ever silently chooses a hosting provider:
1. Applicability: if this install just CREATED AGENTS.md (the replit.md branch or the template branch above), run steps 2–4 to record its Hosting row. If AGENTS.md already existed, run step 5 only (read, classify, report — never write). If no AGENTS.md exists and none was created (the agent.md "No" branch), skip this step — there is nowhere to record.
2. Resolve every Hosting target in the Tech Stack table to exactly ONE read state (per target — a multi-target row is evaluated target by target):
   - s1: no AGENTS.md, no Hosting row, or a blank target (the untouched template placeholder is a blank row and is never parsed as evidence) → run detection (step 3).
   - s2: a non-blank target with NO source= marker → an unevidenced CLAIM, never trusted as fact; detection still runs, and a mismatch between the claim and current config evidence is surfaced, never silently resolved.
   - s3: a source=config:<repo-relative-path> marker whose path still exists in the repo and still supports the recorded label → valid evidence.
   - s4: a source=config: marker whose path is missing, renamed, or no longer supports the label → STALE; treat as s2 and re-flag.
   - s5: a source=user-confirmed:<YYYY-MM-DD> marker → durable; never re-challenged by freshness checks.
   - s6: a validly marked target (s3 or s5) contradicted by NEW target-specific current config evidence → surface the contradiction propose-and-confirm; a user-confirmed target is surfaced as information, never re-flagged as unevidenced. The mere coexistence of another platform's config is not a contradiction.
   - Fail closed: a malformed, unknown-token, multiple-marker, or absolute/non-repo-relative-path marker classifies as s2 — an invalid marker never counts as marked or valid, and never suppresses the evidence review.
3. Detection — scan the two-tier signal list (read each config file once; the .env.example STEP 1 config-files line below draws on the same file set):
   - High-confidence single-platform signals with their labels: railway.toml → Railway, fly.toml → Fly.io, render.yaml → Render, vercel.json → Vercel, netlify.toml → Netlify, wrangler.toml → Cloudflare Workers/Pages, amplify.yml → AWS Amplify
   - Generic/ambiguous signals: Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, Procfile, app.yaml, terraform/, deploy-shaped .github/workflows/ files
   - Discovery scope (resolve the ordered candidate set BEFORE the three-way decision in step 4): candidates are git-TRACKED files only (derive from `git ls-files`; ignored and untracked files never count), matched by signal filename at any depth, EXCLUDING paths under node_modules/, vendor/, dist/, build/, .git/, and directories named test, tests, fixtures, examples, or archive; exclude any path whose realpath resolves outside the repo; duplicate realpaths dedup to ONE candidate. A .github/workflows/ file is deploy-shaped iff the case-insensitive substring "deploy" appears in a job identifier, a step name:, or a uses: action reference — nowhere else (so "deployment" matches; "deploy" appearing only in a comment or any other position does not). terraform/ is a candidate iff at least one git-tracked file exists under a directory named terraform/ (the directory path is the recorded candidate). Signal filenames and exclusion-directory names match case-sensitively. Order candidates by LC_ALL=C repo-relative lexical path order; a duplicate realpath retains its FIRST alias in that order (the retained alias is the source=config: path).
4. Three-way evidence contract, then record. Recording writes ONLY into the AGENTS.md this install just created; a recorded target REPLACES the blank placeholder row, never appends beside it:
   - ZERO evidence → ask the user which platform hosts the project, offering NO default.
   - Exactly ONE unambiguous high-confidence signal → show the evidence (the candidate path and its label) and propose that platform for confirmation.
   - MULTIPLE, generic-only, or conflicting evidence → enumerate everything found and ask the user to confirm one or SEVERAL targets (a split deployment records one Hosting row per target). When AGENTS.md was populated from replit.md, hosting claims found in replit.md are input to this question, never recorded directly as evidence.
   Marker selection is by BASIS OF EVIDENCE, identical for every writer path:
   - source=config:<repo-relative-path> when the recorded label is unambiguously supported by that current config signal. The user's approval of a config-backed proposal authorizes the write but does not change its basis — the marker stays config: and remains freshness-checkable. Several individually-unambiguous high-confidence signals confirmed as several targets each keep their OWN source=config:<its-path>.
   - source=user-confirmed:<YYYY-MM-DD> ONLY when the label comes from the user's own knowledge or choice — config absent, generic, conflicting, or deliberately overridden. Only this user-sourced branch is durable thereafter.
   Serialization (exact): one repeated Hosting row per target, of exactly the form
   | Hosting | <target> | [<free-text note>; ]source=config:<repo-relative-path> |
   or
   | Hosting | <target> | [<free-text note>; ]source=user-confirmed:<YYYY-MM-DD> |
   — the marker token appears exactly once per row, LAST in the Notes cell; each row carries exactly one attributable marker; repo-relative paths render verbatim (spaces stay verbatim inside the cell); the path is ALWAYS repo-relative, never machine-absolute.
   Field hygiene: before writing, any dynamic field (target text, free-text note, or marker path) containing a | character, a source= substring, or a line break/control character is handled deterministically — user-sourced text is REJECTED and re-asked (never escaped, never silently stripped); a config path containing such characters is never serialized into a source=config: marker — show the evidence in the proposal anyway, and on interactive confirmation record source=user-confirmed:<date> instead (the durable user confirmation is the truthfully recordable basis when the path is unrepresentable).
5. If AGENTS.md ALREADY exists (on either install path): never modify it — the never-overwrite rule above stands. Reading its Hosting row for this step is explicitly permitted: resolve each target's state per step 2 (using step 3's scan read-only), then apply step 4's three-way evidence decision READ-ONLY to shape the report — zero evidence: report that no hosting evidence was found and propose NO platform; exactly one unambiguous high-confidence signal: show the evidence and name it as the proposed target; multiple, generic-only, or conflicting evidence: enumerate everything found — never performing step 4's recording action. Report the resolved state, and route any proposed correction or addition to an interactive /document run. On TEMPLATE ONLY — which installs no payloads — first check whether the installed document skill carries the Hosting-evidence rule (grep .claude/skills/document/SKILL.md or .agents/skills/document/SKILL.md for "source=config:"); if it does not, advise running UPDATE ONLY FIRST and then interactive /document — never imply an older document skill can apply the proposal, never refresh payloads from this path, and never mutate the existing AGENTS.md.

For CLAUDE.md:
- If CLAUDE.md does not exist → create the bridge file from the Section 5 template.
- If CLAUDE.md exists and already imports AGENTS.md (contains `@AGENTS.md`) → leave it unchanged.
- If CLAUDE.md exists but does not import AGENTS.md → ask: "I found a CLAUDE.md that does not import AGENTS.md. This workflow uses CLAUDE.md as a tiny bridge that imports AGENTS.md so both Cursor and Claude Code share project context. May I add `@AGENTS.md` to the top of CLAUDE.md? (Yes / No)"
  - If Yes → prepend `@AGENTS.md` to CLAUDE.md preserving existing content below
  - If No → leave it untouched, note that Claude Code will not auto-load AGENTS.md
- Do not duplicate AGENTS.md content into CLAUDE.md.

For CHANGELOG.md:
- If CHANGELOG.md already exists → skip it entirely. Do not read, judge, or touch it.
- Else → create CHANGELOG.md from the Section 5 template.

For .env.example:
- If .env.example already exists → skip it entirely. Do not read, judge, or touch it.
- Else → discover the project's environment variables and create a project-specific
  .env.example. Follow these steps:

  STEP 1 — Collect variable names from all available sources:
  - AGENTS.md — check the Environment Variables table first (preferred: already
    name-only, structured, and documented)
  - .env — if it exists, read variable names only. NEVER copy values. Strip every
    value completely. A line like DATABASE_URL=postgres://... becomes DATABASE_URL=
  - Source code — scan for process.env., import.meta.env., VITE_, NEXT_PUBLIC_, NUXT_,
    os.environ.get(, os.getenv(, dotenv.load_dotenv, config( and similar patterns across
    all project files
  - Config files — check railway.toml, fly.toml, render.yaml, vercel.json, netlify.toml, wrangler.toml, amplify.yml, docker-compose.yml, app.yaml, Procfile, and
    README for any documented variable names. The config files here are the labeled
    subset of the hosting stack step's signal list (same file definitions, read once
    and shared; README is an env-name source only, not a hosting signal); terraform/
    and CI workflow files are deliberately excluded here as poor sources of variable
    NAMES, though they still count for hosting detection.

  STEP 2 — Combine and deduplicate all variable names found across every source.
  A variable found in multiple sources should appear only once.

  STEP 3 — Write .env.example with:
  - Variable names only, all values empty (e.g. DATABASE_URL=)
  - Sensible grouping with comment headers (# Database, # Auth, # App, etc.)
  - A one-line comment on each variable describing its purpose, drawn from
    AGENTS.md documentation if available
  - A note at the top: "# Copy this file to .env and fill in real values locally"
  - NEVER include any real values, tokens, passwords, URLs with credentials, or
    any string that looks like a secret

  STEP 4 — If no variables are found from any source → create .env.example from
  the Section 5 default template instead.

  Tell me how many variables were found and which sources they came from.

--- Documentation Structure Review guidance ---

Classification framework — for each doc or piece of knowledge, classify it as:
- Project briefing / current status → AGENTS.md
- Durable integration or API knowledge → docs/integrations/*.md
- Repeatable testing procedure → docs/testing/*.md
- Durable subsystem / architecture note → docs/build/*.md or docs/architecture/*.md
- Active implementation state / temporary plan history → .cursor/plans/plan-*.md

Rules:
- Do not rewrite or reorganize documentation unless it clearly improves alignment
  with the documentation model above.
- Preserve accurate, useful documentation that already fits its purpose.
- Keep AGENTS.md concise: project briefing, current status, and conditional pointers only.
- Do not move content into docs/ if the project is small enough that a single
  AGENTS.md serves it well. The layered model is for projects that have outgrown
  a single file.
- Before recommending deletion or archival of a plan, confirm any enduring knowledge
  has been migrated elsewhere.
- Prefer review-and-recommend over destructive restructuring when the right
  destination is uncertain.
- Do not invent missing documentation. Base recommendations and edits on the actual
  code and existing docs.

Output format for review:
- Keep as-is — docs that already fit the model
- Move / split — content that belongs in a different location
- Condense — content that is too verbose for its location
- Create — knowledge that needs a dedicated doc that does not exist yet
- Archive candidate — docs or plans that can be retired
- Needs user decision — items where the right action is unclear

After completing the review (or applying changes if option 2), update AGENTS.md
with a Documentation Status section:

## Documentation Status
- Structure version: v22
- Last reviewed: [today's date]
